```sql
WITH tenant_customers AS (
    SELECT c.id,
           c.email,
           c.company,
           c.country_code
      FROM customers c
     WHERE c.tenant_id = %(tenant_id)s
),
order_agg AS (
    SELECT o.customer_id,
           sum(o.total_cents) AS revenue,
           count(*)           AS order_count,
           max(o.created_at)  AS last_order_at
      FROM orders o
      JOIN tenant_customers tc ON tc.id = o.customer_id
     WHERE o.status IN ('paid', 'processing', 'shipped', 'delivered')
     GROUP BY o.customer_id
)
SELECT tc.id,
       tc.email,
       tc.company,
       tc.country_code,
       oa.revenue,
       oa.order_count,
       oa.last_order_at
  FROM tenant_customers tc
  JOIN order_agg oa ON oa.customer_id = tc.id
 WHERE oa.last_order_at >= %(from)s
   AND oa.last_order_at <  %(to)s
 ORDER BY oa.revenue DESC
 LIMIT %(limit)s
```

De originele query aggregeerde eerst alle bestellingen van alle tenants en joinde pas daarna op de tenantfilter, wat leidde tot een nested loop met miljoenen onnodige vergelijkingen. Deze versie filtert eerst op `tenant_id`, aggregeert per klant met `sum`/`count`/`max` in één pass (`max(created_at)` geeft hetzelfde als `DISTINCT ON ... ORDER BY created_at DESC`), en past de datumfilter toe op het geaggregeerde resultaat. De output en ORDER BY blijven gelijk.
